findings.title: String mutation with `<<` corrupts the hostname and can raise on frozen strings
findings.body: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` appends `website_host` into the string literal `"."`. That mutates the literal, which raises FrozenError under frozen-string-literal or on newer Ruby and gives wrong results on older Ruby. It is also easy to misread. Use `discourse_host.ends_with?(".#{website_host}")` instead.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing `?`
findings.body: ActiveModelSerializers looks for `include_website_name?`. The method as written is never called, so `website_name` is always emitted, including for anonymous viewers of TL0 users where `website` is hidden. That leaks the website host. `website_name` is also not added to `untrusted_attributes`, so the restriction is not applied there either. Rename it to `include_website_name?` and also check `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`.

findings.title: Host comparison is case-sensitive and the same-level subdomain branch is wrong
findings.body: `URI(...).host` is not normalised, so `Example.com` will not match the instance hostname. The sibling-subdomain branch compares everything after the first label for hosts with the same number of labels. For `foo.co.uk` against `bar.co.uk`, or an unrelated site such as `a.example.com` against `b.example.com`, it treats them as the same domain. Beyond that, `URI(...).path` is empty for `http://example.com`, and a trailing slash is kept, so the displayed name can end in `/`. The same URI is also re-parsed several times.

findings.title: Missing coverage for edge cases
findings.body: There are no tests for the sibling-subdomain branch, an unparseable website, a blank website, or the anonymous TL0 case. The untrusted-attributes spec does not include `website_name`, so the leak described above goes unnoticed.
